title: Harry Kane told he will claim rare accolades if he leads England to World Cup win | talkSPORT
text:
The Bayern Munich player has been the Three Lions' standout performer in North America, scoring six goals and providing one assist as he leads the team into the quarter-final against Norway.

For generations, the debate over England's greatest-ever player has been reserved for Sir Bobby Charlton, with icons like Wayne Rooney and Gary Lineker following close behind.

However, Kane hasn't just broken milestones, he has shattered them.

At the tournament, the striker has overtaken footballing legends on the World Cup's all-time scoring leaderboard, including Germany's Gerd Muller and Brazil's Pele.

He has also firmly positioned himself in the race for the Golden Boot alongside the world's best players, including Lionel Messi, Erling Haaland, and Kylian Mbappe.

His most recent strike came against Mexico at the Azteca Stadium, where he coolly netted a penalty under immense pressure.

That was his 85th goal for the national team as the England skipper continues to break records for both club and country.

It's rare that footballers receive knighthoods, with David Beckham and Bobby Charlton standing out as two of the extremely lucky ones.

If Kane could deliver this trophy, England's long trophy drought will be over. Better yet, he could also win his second Golden Boot, a feat never accomplished before.

It's not just about  his clinical finishing either. The former Tottenham player has led the Three Lions out for every fixture and has extended his record for the most appearances wearing the captain's armband in the nation's history.

On talkSPORT's World Cup Weekender, Jamie O'Hara and Jermaine Pennant discussed whether Kane would be worthy of the title.

Pennant said: "I don’t think we’ve had anyone better in that position, and at this tournament, it’s the best I’ve seen him.

"Yes, he’s scored goals at other tournaments, but this one for me, he just seems at his absolute best. I think his time at Bayern has really helped him."

Alex Crook added: "I think Wayne Rooney and Kane are two different footballers.

"If you’re asking who’s the better player and has more attributes to his game, it’s Rooney. If you're talking about a predatory goalscorer, you can’t look past Kane.

"I was pondering there, if England were to win the World Cup, do you think we’re going to be talking about Harry Kane as a potential Ballon D'or winner."

Pennant responded: " I think the numbers he has put up in the domestic season, the goals he scored, even in the Champions League were phenomenal.

"If we win the World Cup, it’s Sir Harry Kane from now on."
